scenarios.title: 9:00 AM Logon Storm: Slow Sign-Ins and Black Screens
scenarios.prompt: 120 users sign in between 08:55 and 09:15. Host CPU is 45%, but sign-in takes 90+ seconds and some users get temporary profiles. What is the root cause and primary fix?
choices: Increase session host VM vCPUs from 8 to 16
Standard_LRS Azure Files is IOPS-throttled during the logon burst; move FSLogix profiles to Premium_LRS (FileStorage) sized for burst IOPS or Azure NetApp Files
Switch the host pool load balancing algorithm from Breadth-first to Depth-first
Disable RDP Shortpath on the host pool
scenarios.explanation: FSLogix profile mount/read bursts during a logon storm are IOPS- and latency-bound, not CPU-bound. Standard Azure Files has much lower baseline IOPS and higher tail latency than Premium FileStorage (where provisioned TiB scales IOPS/throughput) or Azure NetApp Files.

scenarios.title: High RTT and Choppy Teams Audio for Remote Users

facts.clientSetup: Corporate laptop running always-on ZTNA/VPN tunnel
facts.avdHostPoolRdpProperties: RDP Shortpath enabled for public networks

scenarios.prompt: Remote users experience high round-trip time and choppy Teams audio. Session hosts are healthy, and RDP Shortpath is enabled on the host pool, yet every session falls back to TCP reverse connect. Why?
choices: RDP Shortpath requires Windows 10 Single-session
The client ZTNA/VPN tunnel is inspecting or blocking outbound UDP / STUN traffic instead of split-tunneling AVD Shortpath endpoints
Entra Kerberos is not enabled on the storage account
The host pool is set to Depth-first load balancing
scenarios.explanation: RDP Shortpath uses UDP (STUN/ICE for public networks or direct UDP for private networks). When a client VPN or ZTNA agent forces all traffic into a TCP tunnel or blocks UDP, AVD silently falls back to TCP reverse connect, increasing latency and jitter.

scenarios.title: Entra-Joined Session Hosts Cannot Mount FSLogix Share

facts.hostJoinType: Microsoft Entra ID joined (no line-of-sight to AD DS)
facts.userIdentities: Hybrid identities synced from AD DS via Entra Connect
facts.storageAuth: None configured on the Azure Files storage account

scenarios.prompt: Your session hosts are pure Microsoft Entra ID joined with no VPN/line-of-sight to domain controllers. Users are hybrid-synced. FSLogix fails to mount \\stcontoso.file.core.windows.net\profiles with Access Denied. What should you configure?
choices: Enable Microsoft Entra Kerberos on the Azure Files storage account and assign Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor RBAC to the AVD users group
Join the storage account to a local workgroup
Switch session hosts to Breadth-first load balancing
Enable Anonymous Read Access on the file share
scenarios.explanation: Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets hybrid-synced users get Kerberos tickets for Azure Files SMB shares from Entra-joined session hosts without line-of-sight to an AD domain controller—paired with Azure RBAC (Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor) and NTFS permissions.

scenarios.title: Choosing Between Pooled AVD, Personal AVD, and Windows 365

facts.groupA: 400 task workers using browser + M365 Apps on shift schedules
facts.groupB: 25 developers needing local admin, custom SDKs, and predictable flat monthly pricing

scenarios.prompt: How should you place Group A and Group B according to Desktop DevOps workload placement principles?
choices: Put both groups on Personal AVD with static 24/7 VMs
Put Group A on Pooled AVD (Windows 11 Multi-session + Scaling Plan) and Group B on Windows 365 Enterprise (or Personal AVD if GPU/custom Azure VNet control is required)
Put Group A on Windows 365 Frontline Dedicated and Group B on Pooled AVD
Put both groups on a single validation host pool
scenarios.explanation: Shift/task workers with standard apps get the best cost density on Pooled AVD multi-session with autoscale. Persistent developers who need dedicated compute, local admin, and predictable per-user licensing fit Windows 365 Enterprise (or Personal AVD when specialized Azure VM SKUs/GPUs are needed).

scenarios.title: Autoscale Stopped All Hosts Overnight—Morning Users Blocked
scenarios.prompt: To save cost, an autoscale plan deallocates all session hosts overnight. Early-bird users trying to sign in before the morning ramp-up window get 'No available resources'. What single setting fixes this?
choices: Set the host pool to Validation Environment = True
Enable Start VM on Connect on the host pool (and ensure the AVD service principal has the Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor role)
Change the scaling plan time zone to UTC
Switch FSLogix to Cloud Cache
scenarios.explanation: When a scaling plan scales down to 0 active hosts off-peak, Start VM on Connect lets AVD automatically boot a deallocated host when a user connects—provided the Azure Virtual Desktop service principal has the Desktop Virtualization Power On Contributor RBAC role.

scenarios.title: Private Endpoint Deployed, But Storage Still Resolves Publicly

facts.nslookupFromSessionHost: Resolves to 52.x.x.x (public IP) and SMB mount fails

scenarios.prompt: You disabled public access on the FSLogix storage account and created a Private Endpoint, but session hosts still resolve the public IP and fail to mount profiles. What is the fix?
choices: Re-enable public network access on the storage account
Create/link the privatelink.file.core.windows.net Private DNS Zone (with an A record for the private IP) to the spoke/hub VNet
Switch from Premium_LRS to Standard_LRS
Enable Start VM on Connect
scenarios.explanation: Without a Private DNS Zone (privatelink.file.core.windows.net) linked to the VNet (or forwarded via DNS Private Resolver), session hosts receive the public DNS CNAME/IP and get blocked by the storage firewall.

scenarios.title: Workstation Sleep Policy Breaks Pooled Session Hosts

facts.hostJoinType: Microsoft Entra ID joined + Intune enrolled
facts.symptom: Pooled Windows 11 Multi-session hosts go unresponsive after 30 minutes of idle time
facts.intuneAssignment: Corporate Workstation Power Policy assigned to 'All Devices'

scenarios.prompt: Pooled AVD session hosts enrolled in Intune randomly drop into sleep/hibernate, disconnecting active users. What is the cleanest fix?
choices: Unenroll all session hosts from Intune
Use an Intune Assignment Filter to exclude Windows 11 Multi-session (or AVD host prefixes) from workstation power/sleep policies and apply an AVD-specific baseline
Set maxSessionLimit to 1
Disable Entra SSO
scenarios.explanation: Workstation power/sleep policies should never apply to AVD session hosts. Intune Assignment Filters cleanly separate multi-session AVD hosts from physical laptops.

scenarios.title: Pool Never Scales to Zero After Hours

facts.scalingPlan: Ramp-down 18:00 (capacity threshold 90%, force sign-out off, stop hosts only when they have no active or disconnected sessions); off-peak from 20:00 inherits the threshold
facts.at22h00OffPeak: 0 active sessions, 14 disconnected sessions, 2 hosts running
facts.hostPolicy: No time limit set for disconnected sessions

scenarios.prompt: Every night two hosts stay running until morning even though nobody is working. What explains it, and what is the fix that keeps force sign-out off?
choices: Disconnected sessions hold the hosts; set a 15 to 30 minute disconnected-session time limit on the hosts
The scaling plan isn't assigned to the host pool, so off-peak settings never apply; assign it
Breadth-first load balancing prevents deallocation; switch off-peak to depth-first
Start VM on Connect restarts hosts after autoscale stops them; turn it off
scenarios.explanation: The plan only stops hosts with no active or disconnected sessions, and consolidation counts disconnected sessions too: CEILING(14 / (8 x 0.9)) = 2 hosts. With single sign-on, a lock also disconnects. A disconnected-session time limit signs those users out so the pool can reach zero.

scenarios.title: Admins On-Premises Can't Reach the Profile Share's Private Endpoint

facts.topology: Hub-spoke, ExpressRoute to on-premises, profile storage public network access disabled
facts.privateDnsZone: privatelink.file.core.windows.net, linked to the hub VNet
facts.onPremLookup: Resolves storage name to a public address; SMB times out

scenarios.prompt: Session hosts mount the FSLogix share fine, but admins on-premises can't open it to fix a corrupt profile. What is the root cause and fix?
choices: The private endpoint sits in its own subnet instead of the session host subnet; move it next to the hosts
Enable public network access on the storage account
Link the private DNS zone to the ExpressRoute gateway subnet so on-premises queries see it
168.63.129.16 is unreachable from on-premises; forward to a DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint in the hub
scenarios.explanation: 168.63.129.16 only answers from inside Azure, so the on-premises forwarder fails and falls back to public resolution. An inbound endpoint gives on-premises DNS a private IP that answers from the zones linked to the hub.

scenarios.title: Ephemeral OS Disk Pool Fails Its Nightly Scale-Down

facts.poolType: Pooled, session host configuration, ephemeral OS disk on temp disk
facts.activityLog: Deallocate operations on session hosts fail every night at ramp-down

scenarios.prompt: After moving a pooled host pool to ephemeral OS disks, the nightly ramp-down errors and hosts stay on. What change fits the design?
choices: Switch the OS disk back to Premium SSD so hosts can hibernate
Raise the ramp-down capacity threshold to 100% so fewer hosts are chosen for deallocation
Dynamic autoscaling with 100% minimum active hosts in every phase, so it creates and deletes hosts
Enable Azure Backup on the session hosts before deallocation
scenarios.explanation: Hosts on ephemeral OS disks can't be deallocated. Microsoft's guidance is dynamic autoscaling with 100% minimum active hosts, so scaling only creates and deletes hosts. Azure Backup isn't supported on ephemeral OS disks.
